research_mode: official UK government and ONS primary statistical publications and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Guide purpose
verified_claims: The guide explains youth-justice data sources, quality, methodology, concepts and definitions.
limitations: The guide does not itself provide a verified parcel result.

sources.name: Annual and monthly products
verified_claims: The guide covers both annual youth-justice statistics and monthly youth-custody data.
limitations: The products use different frequencies and should remain separately labelled.

sources.name: Administrative data sources
verified_claims: Youth-justice statistics rely on several administrative databases and bespoke collections.
limitations: Administrative sources can contain late updates and classification differences.

sources.name: Child age definition
verified_claims: Youth-justice statistics generally define children as ages 10 to 17.
limitations: Some tables may include 18-year-olds and must state that explicitly.

sources.name: First-time-entrant definition
verified_claims: A first-time entrant is a child receiving a first caution or court sentence while resident in England and Wales.
limitations: Diversionary outcomes not recorded as cautions or sentences may not create an FTE.

sources.name: Proven-offence definition
verified_claims: A proven offence is one resulting in a caution or conviction.
limitations: The definition excludes allegations without a proven disposal.

sources.name: Reoffending follow-up
verified_claims: Proven reoffending uses a defined follow-up and waiting period.
limitations: Recent cohorts cannot be compared before follow-up is complete.

sources.name: Custody snapshot basis
verified_claims: Monthly custody statistics describe children in the secure estate at specified points or periods.
limitations: A custody snapshot is not a flow of admissions or releases.

sources.name: Remand distinction
verified_claims: Youth custody data distinguish remand from sentenced detention.
limitations: Remand does not imply conviction for the charge concerned.

sources.name: Source-period differences
verified_claims: Different chapters can use financial years, calendar years or cohort periods.
limitations: Figures must not be merged without period alignment.

sources.name: Guide rounding boundary
verified_claims: Published commentary may use rounded values while supplementary tables retain more precision.
limitations: Recalculations should use underlying unrounded tables where available.

sources.name: Ethnicity quality boundary
verified_claims: Ethnicity reporting can include unknown values and different identification bases.
limitations: Unknown ethnicity must not be imputed without documented methodology.

sources.name: Local-data boundary
verified_claims: Youth justice service level tables support local analysis.
limitations: Service-area figures do not identify individual children or exact offence locations.

sources.name: Offence-group classification
verified_claims: The guide documents changes in offence grouping for the 2024 to 2025 publication.
limitations: Trend analysis must respect classification breaks.

sources.name: Multiple-system reconciliation
verified_claims: The annual report draws on systems managed by different agencies.
limitations: Cross-source totals may not reconcile because units and extraction dates differ.

sources.name: Quality-assurance role
verified_claims: Data providers and analysts apply validation and quality checks before publication.
limitations: Quality assurance reduces but does not eliminate recording error.

sources.name: Revision boundary
verified_claims: Youth-justice data may be revised when improved information becomes available.
limitations: Release date and version should be retained in evidence.

sources.name: Adult-comparison caution
verified_claims: Youth and adult justice statistics use related but not always identical concepts and populations.
limitations: Rates should not be ranked without demographic and offence-mix adjustment.

sources.name: Disclosure boundary
verified_claims: Published statistics use aggregation and disclosure controls to protect children.
limitations: The data cannot be used to reconstruct a named child or exact case.

sources.name: Business-use boundary
verified_claims: The guide provides methodology, not a property-level safety score.
limitations: No parcel or business value should be generated without separate spatial evidence.
